author: Caroline Bowyer
title: CMPD conducting proactive home visits for at-risk youth - NewsBreak
text:
By Caroline Bowyer ,
1 hours ago
CHARLOTTE, N.C. ( QUEEN CITY NEWS ) — Charlotte-Mecklenburg Police officers are doing proactive home visits as the July Fourth holiday approaches.
It’s a move to get ahead of safety risks that often happen around holidays and when kids are out of school. The Juvenile Priority Offender Strategy Team, also known as JPOST, specializes in dealing with children at risk of becoming repeat offenders.
“Kids are out of school,” said Officer Emma Bellamy. “They’re bored. They’re trying to find anything to occupy themselves, to entertain themselves.”
Sometimes that lack of structure leads to bad decisions, like participating in teen street takeovers or resorting to gun violence.
“Just one silly decision can have a long-lasting outcome,” said Bellamy.
Officer Bellamy is one of the people trying to reach these kids before that happens. She’s one of four JPOST officers, who will conduct between 30 and 40 homes visits this week. They’re checking on young people who’ve recently been charged or were charged this time last year.
“To reiterate to them the safety concerns of this weekend, to make good decisions, and to also remind parents that there’s a possibility that they can be held accountable for their children’s decisions,” she said.
The point of the home visits is to build relationships with these families and connect them to resources.
“Where there’s trust and communication, those strong partnerships help give the youth the best chance at succeeding,” said Bellamy.
She has been doing this for about a year now and says the parents typically appreciate the efforts. She’s already seen the difference they can make.
“We celebrate these small wins,” said Bellamy. “If that means a juvenile getting a job or finishing the school year or finishing high school, getting their diploma, or their alternatives, getting their GED. “There have definitely been several success stories.”
